report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of daedalus/mapping/reach.py: defines helper functions for import record extraction, toplevel name collection, module-level binding mapping, shim detection, and the _scan function.
risks: _toplevel_names | medium | Docstring claims descends into if/try for conditional definitions but code also descends into With and AsyncWith, and only up to depth < 3. | Check if With/AsyncWith should be included per spec.

_module_level_bindings | medium | Docstring claims 'MODULE LEVEL ONLY' is load-bearing but code does not enforce it; it only processes top-level statements. | Add assertion or comment to clarify enforcement.

_shim_body | medium | Docstring says 'no def, no class' but code does not check for def/class explicitly; it returns False on non-import/assign/if/try statements, which would catch def/class. | Verify that def/class are indeed caught by the final return False.

_shim_body | medium | Docstring mentions '__all__' but code only allows Assign with target being a Name, not a tuple or list; __all__ is often assigned to a list. | Check if __all__ = [...] is considered a plain alias assignment.
_scan | low | Function uses _py_dotted(rel) which is not defined in this chunk; its behavior is uncheckable. | Ensure _py_dotted is defined elsewhere.

symbols.name: _toplevel_names
symbols.note: Returns set of names bound at module import time, descending into if/try/with/asyncwith up to depth 2.

symbols.name: _module_level_bindings
symbols.note: Returns dict mapping bound name to list of records for module-level imports only.

symbols.name: _shim_body
symbols.note: Returns True if body re-exports only (no def/class/executable statements beyond imports, __all__, plain alias assignments).

symbols.name: _scan
symbols.note: Parses text into _Src with tree, records, weak, is_shim, toplevel, and string constants.

claims.text: LIVE import records only. Weak ones are reachable only via :func:`_split_imports`, so no caller can pick them up by accident.
claims.why: The claim references _split_imports which is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify that weak records are only reachable via that function.

claims.text: Names a module binds at import time. Descends one level into ``if`` and ``try`` because conditional definitions are ordinary in this codebase.
claims.why: The code descends into if, try, with, and asyncwith, not just if and try. Also descends up to depth < 3, not just one level (depth 0 becomes depth 1, etc.).

claims.text: MODULE LEVEL ONLY, and that restriction is load-bearing. cli.py's branches all write ``from .doctor import main as m`` / ``from .benchmark import main as m`` -- the SAME local name ``m`` in sixty different branches. Binding names from every scope made ``m`` resolve to all sixty modules, so every subcommand appeared to reach every other subcommand's target and the whole dispatch collapsed into one blob. A branch's own imports are handled separately, from that branch's own records.
claims.why: The claim refers to cli.py and specific import patterns not present in this chunk; cannot verify the behavior of branch imports or the collapse scenario.

claims.text: True when the module body re-exports and does nothing else. Detected structurally, never guessed: no def, no class, no executable statement beyond imports, ``__all__`` and plain alias assignments. A shim is worth naming because it is the one module class where 'nothing reaches it' is expected rather than alarming.
claims.why: The code does not explicitly check for def/class; it returns False on any statement that is not Import, ImportFrom, Assign (with specific conditions), Try, If, or Expr (first line only). This catches def/class implicitly, but the docstring claims 'no def, no class' as a structural detection, which is misleading. Also, the code allows __all__ only if assigned to a Name, List, Tuple, or Attribute, but the docstring says 'plain alias assignments' which might be interpreted differently.

claims.text: Parses text into _Src with tree, records, weak, is_shim, toplevel, and string constants.
claims.why: The code sets src.tree, src.records, src.weak, src.is_shim, src.toplevel, and then walks for string constants.

observations.what: _toplevel_names descends into With and AsyncWith in addition to If and Try, and allows depth up to 2 (depth < 3).
_module_level_bindings does not enforce 'MODULE LEVEL ONLY' beyond processing only top-level statements; no guard against being called with non-module tree.

_shim_body returns False on any statement that is not Import, ImportFrom, Assign (with specific target/value types), Try, If, or Expr (first line only). It does not explicitly check for def/class, but they would be caught by the final return False.
_scan uses _py_dotted(rel) which is not defined in this chunk.
